title: The future seen from the past
summary: Как говорить о «будущем в прошедшем»: **would, was/were going to, was/were to, was about to, past continuous** и несбывшиеся планы с **was/were to have, was going to have**.
ru:
## О чём этот юнит
Когда мы рассказываем о прошлом, у событий тоже есть «своё будущее»: то, что тогда ещё предстояло. Русский язык это почти не выделяет («Он не знал, что станет знаменитым»). В английском для такого «будущего в прошедшем» есть набор форм, и выбор зависит от того, был ли это план, прогноз, расписание или судьба — и осуществилось ли задуманное.

## Would: самое нейтральное
**would + инфинитив** — прогноз и обещание в рассказе или косвенной речи; часто в литературном повествовании о том, что случилось позже:
> He promised that he **would** help us. — Он обещал, что поможет нам.
> She never imagined she **would** return twenty years later. — Она и представить не могла, что вернётся через двадцать лет.
**would have + причастие** — к определённому моменту в прошлом что-то будет завершено:
> I knew we **would have** spent all the money by June. — Я знал, что к июню мы потратим все деньги.

## Was/were going to: намерение и признаки
**was/were going to + инфинитив** — намерение или план в прошлом. Часто (но не обязательно) значит, что намерение **не осуществилось**:
> I **was going to** call you, but I forgot. — Я собирался тебе позвонить, но забыл.
> It **was going to** rain — you could see it in the sky. — Собирался дождь, это было видно по небу.
Нельзя заменить такое намерение на would: ~~I would call you, but I forgot.~~ → I **was going to** call you.

## Was/were to и was/were to have
**was/were to + инфинитив** — запланированное или «суждено». **was/were to have + причастие** — запланированное, но не состоявшееся:
> The play **was to open** in May. — Премьера была намечена на май. (состоялась)
> The play **was to have opened** in May. — Премьеру планировали на май (но она не состоялась).
> He **was to become** a world champion. — Ему предстояло стать чемпионом мира. (судьба)

## Past continuous и was about to
**Past continuous** передаёт заранее оговорённый план на ближайшее будущее с точки зрения прошлого:
> I couldn't stay — I **was meeting** Julia at five. — Я не мог остаться: у меня была встреча с Джулией в пять.
**was/were about to** — «собирался, и тут...»:
> We **were just about to** leave when it started to rain. — Мы уже собирались выходить, когда начался дождь.

## Типичные ошибки
- ~~I would phone, but I forgot.~~ → I **was going to** phone, but I forgot. (несбывшееся намерение)
- ~~She said she will come.~~ → She said she **would come**. (согласование времён)
- ~~The concert was to be on Monday but it was cancelled.~~ → …**was to have been** on Monday… (если подчёркиваем, что не состоялось)
- Фраза «I was to meet him next Friday» в бытовом разговоре звучит слишком официально; обычно: I **was meeting** him / I **was going to meet** him.
en:
## What this unit is about
When we tell a story set in the past, events have their own 'future': things that were still to come at that moment. English uses several forms for this 'future in the past'. The choice depends on whether it was a plan, a prediction, a timetable or fate, and on whether the plan actually happened.

## Would: the neutral choice
**would + infinitive** — prediction or promise in a story or in reported speech:
> He promised that he **would** help us.
> She never imagined she **would** return twenty years later.
**would have + past participle** — something will be finished by a point in the past:
> I knew we **would have** spent all the money by June.

## Was/were going to: intention and evidence
**was/were going to + infinitive** shows an intention or plan in the past. It often (not always) means the plan was **not carried out**:
> I **was going to** call you, but I forgot.
> It **was going to** rain — you could see it in the sky.
We cannot use would for an unfulfilled intention: ~~I would call you, but I forgot.~~ → I **was going to** call you.

## Was/were to and was/were to have
**was/were to + infinitive** — planned, or destined. **was/were to have + past participle** — planned but it did not happen:
> The play **was to open** in May. (it did)
> The play **was to have opened** in May. (it did not)
> He **was to become** a world champion. (destiny)

## Past continuous and was about to
**Past continuous** for an arrangement:
> I couldn't stay — I **was meeting** Julia at five.
**was/were about to** — on the point of doing something when something interrupted:
> We **were just about to** leave when it started to rain.

## Common mistakes
- ~~I would phone, but I forgot.~~ → I **was going to** phone, but I forgot.
- ~~She said she will come.~~ → She said she **would come**.
- If the event did not happen, use **was to have + V3**, not was to + V.
structure:
## Формулы
| Смысл | Форма | Пример |
|---|---|---|
| прогноз, обещание | **would** + V | He said he **would** call. |
| завершится к моменту | **would have** + V3 | She knew she **would have** finished by noon. |
| намерение, план | was/were **going to** + V | I **was going to** write. |
| признаки | was/were **going to** + V | The ship **was going to** sink. |
| официальный план | was/were **to** + V | The summit **was to** open on Monday. |
| судьба | was/were **to** + V | He **was to** die far from home. |
| не состоялось | was/were **to have** + V3 | It **was to have been** ready in May. |
| не состоялось | was/were **going to have** + V3 | We **were going to have** left by six. |
| договорённость | was/were **-ing** | I **was meeting** Tom at six. |
| вот-вот | was/were **about to** + V | She **was about to** speak. |

## Сравнение: форма, смысл, пример
| Форма | Смысл | Пример |
|---|---|---|
| I **was going to** buy it | намерение (обычно не сбылось) | I was going to buy it, but it was sold. |
| I **would** buy it | в рассказе: так и сделал / гипотеза | He said he would buy it. |
| It **was to have** opened | запланировано, не состоялось | It was to have opened in May. |
| It **was to open** | запланировано, состоялось | It was to open in May, and it did. |

## Отрицание и вопрос
> I **wasn't going to** tell him, but I **did**.
> She said she **wouldn't** go. / **Were** you **going to** say something?
> **Was** the meeting **to** take place on Friday? — Yes, it was.

exercises.title: Будущее в прошедшем
exercises.instruction: Вставьте подходящую форму. Допустимые варианты перечислены в ответе, поэтому засчитывается любой верный.

items.text: She didn't know then that the decision {{would|was going to|was to}} change her life.
items.hint: would / was going to / was to

items.text: I {{was going to|was planning to}} call you earlier, but my battery died.
We were just {{about to|going to}} sit down to dinner when the lights went out.
I knew that I {{would have|'d have}} finished the report by Friday if nothing went wrong.
Little did they suspect that within a year the company {{would|was going to|was to}} be bankrupt.
items.hint: would / was going to / was to

items.text: My brother said he {{was leaving|was going to leave|would leave}} for Canada the following week.
The ceremony {{was to have|was going to have}} taken place on Monday, but it was cancelled.

exercises.title: Намерения, которые не сбылись
exercises.instruction: Вставьте форму was/were going to, would, would have и т. п. по смыслу.

items.text: I {{was going to|was planning to}} tell her the truth, but I lost my nerve.
We {{weren't going to|were not going to}} mention the price, but she asked directly.
He {{was about to|was going to}} sign the contract when his lawyer phoned.
She said she {{wouldn't|would not}} help us, and she didn't.
I had hoped the work {{would have|would've}} been finished by now.
I wondered whether we {{would}} ever see each other again.

items.q: 'Did you phone Anna?' 'No, I ___, but I forgot.'
items.why: Несбывшееся намерение в прошлом → **was going to**.

items.q: In 1998 she left home, never imagining that she ___ twenty years later as the mayor.
items.why: В рассказе о прошлом будущее передаётся через **would**.

items.q: I couldn't stay long because I ___ Julia later that afternoon.
items.why: Договорённость с точки зрения прошлого → **was meeting**.

items.q: The new stadium ___ opened last May, but there were long delays.
items.why: Не состоявшийся план → **was to have + V3**.

items.q: By the time they got home, she knew the film ___ already.
items.why: К моменту в прошлом уже начнётся → **would have + V3**.

items.q: He ___ leave when the manager walked in.
I knew that by midnight I ___ in bed.
items.why: Действие в процессе в момент в будущем (с точки зрения прошлого) → **would be + -ing**.

items.q: В каком предложении мост НЕ был достроен в мае?
options: The bridge was to be finished in May.
The bridge was to have been finished in May.
The bridge would finish in May.
items.why: **was to have been** — план не осуществился.

items.q: Какое предложение естественно в рассказе о судьбе героя?
options: He didn't know then that he would meet his wife on that train.
He didn't know then that he will meet his wife on that train.
He doesn't know then that he would meet his wife.

items.q: Какое предложение неверно, если речь о НЕсбывшемся намерении?
options: I was going to call you.
I would call you, but I forgot.
I was about to call you.
items.why: Несбывшееся намерение в прошлом выражается через **was going to**, а не **would**.

items.q: 'I was meeting Tom at six' означает:
options: У меня была договорённость встретиться с Томом в шесть.
Я встретился с Томом в шесть.
Я каждый день встречался с Томом в шесть.
items.why: Past continuous передаёт запланированное будущее с точки зрения прошлого.
В прошлом (thought) мы смотрим вперёд: **would rain**.

items.q: 'He was just about to speak when the lights went out' подразумевает:
items.why: **was about to ... when** — действие было прервано, не начавшись.

exercises.title: Перепишите в прошедшем
exercises.instruction: Перепишите предложение с использованием указанной формы.

items.prompt: 'I'm going to resign,' she said. → She said she ... (was going to)
answers: She said she was going to resign.
She said that she was going to resign.

items.prompt: 'I'll help you,' he promised. → He promised that he ... (would)
answers: He promised that he would help me.
He promised he would help me.
He promised that he'd help me.

items.prompt: The meeting was planned for Friday but did not take place. (was to have) → The meeting ... (take place)
answers: The meeting was to have taken place on Friday.

items.prompt: I intended to buy a car. (was going to) → I ...
answers: I was going to buy a car.
I was going to buy a car, but I changed my mind.

items.prompt: She had an appointment with the dentist later that day. (past continuous) → She ... (see the dentist)
answers: She was seeing the dentist later that day.

items.prompt: We were on the point of leaving when it began to rain. (about to) → We ...
answers: We were about to leave when it began to rain.
We were just about to leave when it began to rain.

exercises.title: Напишите о себе
exercises.instruction: Ответьте полными предложениями, используя «будущее в прошедшем».

items.prompt: Write about something you were going to do last weekend but didn't.
items.sample: I was going to clean the flat last weekend, but I went to the cinema instead.

items.prompt: Write about a moment when you were just about to do something and something interrupted you.
items.sample: I was just about to fall asleep when my neighbour started drilling.

items.prompt: Complete: 'When I was a child, I never imagined that I would ...'
items.sample: When I was a child, I never imagined that I would live in another country.

items.prompt: Write about a plan you had last month (use past continuous).
items.sample: Last month I was visiting my parents every weekend because my father was ill.

items.prompt: Describe an event that was to have happened but was cancelled or postponed.
items.sample: Our company party was to have taken place in December, but it was postponed until January.

items.prompt: Write about something you were planning to do before an unexpected event stopped you.
items.sample: I was going to start a new job in May, but the company went bankrupt.
